articleTitle: Pilot Study on Lighting Environment and Organizational Productivity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The lighting design for future office spaces should not only ensure visual workability, but also enhance the employees’ productivity, creativity, satisfaction and etc. that would generate the value of working in face to face in office buildings. The purpose of this study is to identify the criteria for evaluating the visual environment of office space in terms of the organizational productivity to be addressed in office visual design. The results of the image evaluation experiment to extract the visual elements and lighting conditions that are required for several different types of office activity are reported.

articleTitle: Associations Between Daytime Light Exposure and Mood, Vitality, Work Efficiency, and Sleep: A Field Study in Offices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This field study investigates the associations between office employees’ daytime light exposure and their experiences and behavior across multiple days. The study recruited 15 participants in real office environments and lasted for three weeks. Light exposure was recorded using wearable light sensors, sleep data were collected via wristbands, and experiences were gathered through four questionnaires every in-office working day. The analysis revealed that higher average illuminance over the past half-hour was positively related to self-reported positive affect, vitality, and work efficiency. Illuminance above 250 lx significantly improved vitality and morning work efficiency. Additionally, longer time exposed to illuminance above 250 lx during the day also facilitated quicker sleep onset at night. This study provides empirical evidence of the positive effects of bright daytime light exposure on office employees’ performance and sleep.

articleTitle: Quality Assessment: Luminance Distribution Analysis in an Urban Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The lack of comprehensive quality assessment of urban lighting results in discrete and unbalanced luminance levels, negatively affecting visual perception for both drivers and pedestrians. This underscores the importance of research aimed at developing methods for a holistic assessment of luminance distribution within the field of view. A methodology was developed for measuring luminance parameters in urban environments by integrating empirical measurements with calculated data, accounting for changes in visual perception under mesopic conditions. The data processing algorithm applies mesopic photometry principles, considering both the spectral characteristics of light sources and shifts in visual spectral sensitivity in low-light conditions.

articleTitle: Different Materials Sealing Technology and Its Application in the Preparation of Various Light Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This paper briefly introduces the basic principle and methods of sealing technology of different materials. Taking AgCu brazing and AuSn eutectic welding as examples, the application of different materials sealing technology in the manufacture of pulsed xenon lamp and LED (Light Emitting Diode) light source is described, and the effect of this technology on the reliability of the light source after it is used in the manufacture of the two light sources.

articleTitle: Caravaggio’s mastery as a modern lighting designer’s reflection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio’s celebrated work happens to be the result of a perceptual education that he received in Milan and to the continuous pursuing of his quest for skills in Rome. He improved his technique in such a way that, according to G.P.Bellori, painters "praised him as the unique imitator of nature, and looked his work as miracles". The mastery of light he progressively gained during this period, led him to innovate in terms of optical solutions he adopted controlling the light dispersion in his studio through the reflectance of his environment.

articleTitle: Survey on People’s Opinions Regarding Façade Lighting and Light Pollution: The Case Study of Greece
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Light pollution is part of the contemporary environmental crisis that threatens directly and indirectly humans and biodiversity. This phenomenon has been deteriorating the last years. Scientists have given the last decades prominence to the need for proper urban lighting design, including buildings’ façade lighting, that causes less light pollution and energy consumption. Based on the available literature and research, façade lighting significantly contributes to the increase of the night sky glow near cities. Being part of the general urban lighting, façade lighting has not been studied though sufficiently concerning its impact on light pollution. In addition, the absence of strict restrictions applied on light pollution caused by façade lighting has been observed at global scale. This paper relies on a survey related to different existent façade lighting installations applied on modern buildings in Greece. The objective of this paper is the collection and comparison between gathered qualitative and quantitative data concerning the waste of light caused by façade lighting that is emitted towards unwanted directions such as sky or adjacent building properties. The aim of this research is the assessment of different façade lighting techniques regarding light pollution and energy waste.

articleTitle: Securing Additional Energy Savings in SSL: an International Lighting Technology Roadmap
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Over the past 20 years, the development and adoption of-state lighting (SSL) has led to substantial improvements in the quality and efficiency of lighting. This disruptive technology enabled a decoupling of lighting and energy consumption, whereby delivered lumens of light around the world has increased while lighting-related energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions have decreased. But substantial further savings are possible through further improvements in LED efficacy and more widespread adoption of smart lighting systems and controls. To help capture these further savings, a joint effort to develop an international lighting technology roadmap is being launched by the IEEE Smart Lighting Program, the IEA 4E SSLC Platform and the International Solid-State Lighting Association (ISA). This paper describes the scope of this roadmap and highlights some of the major challenges in achieving the full potential for SSL in the second quarter of this century.

articleTitle: The Effects of Natural Landscape Images Using Projector Display on Human Psychophysiology in Rest Space
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: We aim to create a comfortable environment with low fatigue by investigating the psychological and physiological effects of projected natural landscape images on individuals in rest areas. Our experiment primarily focuses on image type and considers greenery view rate, dynamic/static nature, and view as key parameters. Results indicate the absence of visual fatigue at critical flicker fusion fluctuation rates of 3 or less. Psychological evaluations reveal that "sense of healing" and "calmness" decrease with abrupt image movements or minimal greenery. Further, the sense of oppression increased in poorly lit environments and decreased in well-lit ones. Our findings suggest that the projection of natural landscape images can help create comfortable rest areas when implemented under appropriate conditions.

articleTitle: KNX-based Lighting System Controlled by Brain Signals (EEG)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This paper presents an assistive system for controlling different light sources throw brain signals. The aim is to improve home automation systems specially the lighting systems by developing an interface to integrate the KNX-based lighting systems with brain signals. The proposed system consists of three parts. The first part is for detecting the EEG signals from the brain cortex. The second part is the heart of our research which represents a gateway that receives the detected EEG signals, analyses them, generates appropriate KNX commands, and sends these commands to the final part of the proposed system which is the Lighting System (LS) that implemented using KNX protocol. After testing the proposed system against different persons, the results showed the system correctly response to the user actions from 68 to 80 % of the total issued signals, according to the brain headset used, hardware processing resources that implement the gateway and the environment factors that effect of the brain signals.

articleTitle: Influence of AC Power Supply on Light Flicker Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Accurate measurement of the short-term flicker indicator is important for avoiding visible flicker and for SSL products to comply with regulations. The IC2023 Interlaboratory Comparison of temporal light modulation measurements revealed large variations depending on the laboratory-grade AC power supplies used. A technical study using a halogen lamp was carried out, resulting in 45 measurements covering 19 different manufacturers of AC power supplies. It demonstrated large differences of measured values of more than one order of magnitude and a correlation with low frequency components is found. A new method to estimate the low frequency noise of a specific power supply and its influence on the measured short term flicker indicator is proposed. Setting a limit for this of 0.03 would make 50% of the power supplies in our sample fail. Laboratories can use this method to evaluate the suitability of their specific AC power supply, to determine their influence on short term flicker indicator measurements, and to support measurement uncertainty estimation.

articleTitle: Pedestrian Response to Sustainable Outdoor Lighting: A Field Study with Elderly Participants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: In an effort to reduce the negative ecological impact of outdoor lighting, amber and warm white light sources and delimited light distributions are currently being tested. This study investigates elderly pedestrians’ acceptance and preference for sustainable outdoor lighting in a field test along a pedestrian/bicycle path. Settings with three different correlated color temperatures (1800 K- amber, 2200 K and 3000 K), each with two different types of optics (regular and delimited light distributions) were evaluated. The results show that the satisfaction with the regular light distribution was significantly higher than with the delimited. The light with a correlated color temperature of 2200 K in combination with a regular light distribution was most preferred. When asked about accepting amber lighting on a pedestrian/bicycle path, 53% were positive, 23.5% said no and 23.5% were unsure.

articleTitle: Investigating the POLQ to Assess Quality of Outdoor Urban Lighting for Pedestrians in the Context of Lighting Levels Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The "POLQ" is a tool for assessing the quality of outdoor lighting. To the best of our knowledge, this scale has never been translated into French, although it could offer interesting practical and scientific prospects. The aim of this field study is to investigate the use of POLQ to assess the lighting quality for pedestrians under various reduced lighting conditions, and to explore its links with visual accessibility and perceived safety. Results highlighted that the French translation only retrieves one dimension of the initial POLQ (the "Perceived Strength Quality"), and this dimension indeed discriminates between lighting conditions, while being slightly related to visual accessibility and perceived safety. The others dimensions found are promising towards a generic tool for assessing lighting quality for pedestrians.

articleTitle: Integrative Lighting Design of a Living Area in a Residential Care Facility
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Integrative lighting design takes into account several factors: spectrum, intensity, and timing of lighting, but also the materials of the room. In this paper, the integrative lighting design of a living area in a residential care facility is described. The residents are elderly people with dementia. They can benefit from more light at eye level in the morning and dimmed lighting in the (late) afternoon and evening, which could lead to better sleep, mental health, and behaviour. The lighting calculations in DIALux evo show that with the right materials and luminaires, it is possible to achieve a melanopic EDI of more than 500 lx at the residents' positions.

articleTitle: Electrical and Optical Simulation of Organic Light-Emitting Devices: The Role of Emissive Layer Thickness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Optimizing the performance of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) containing a dopant in the emissive layer (EML), requires the coupling of electrical and optical simulations to design device structures before proceeding to fabrication. Electrical or optical simulation alone, is not sufficient to properly optimize an OLED structure. By adjusting the conditions at the interlayer interfaces, taking into account defect states in the organic layers and controlling the thickness of the doped emissive layer in the ITO/NPB/Alq3(1%)/Alq3/LiF/Al structure, the performance of five different devices with different emissive layer thicknesses (15, 30, 45, 60, and 75 nm) has been studied. Structure characteristics analyzed included current density-voltage relationships, luminance-current density, position-recombination rate and electroluminescence spectrum. According to the results obtained, increasing the thickness of the emissive layer (EML) leads to a decrease in current density and turn-on voltage, affects the recombination rate and, consequently, the luminance and light spectrum, while the device with 30 nm thick EML has a clearer and higher maximum emission intensity than the other devices.

articleTitle: The Social Light Field at Illuminated Footpaths
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The light field describes the light in a given space, capturing spatial and form-giving visual qualities of light, such as the direction and diffuseness, in addition to conventional intensity-related metrics. In urban mobility, this is connected to social aspects, as these lighting qualities impact how objects or people appear. We tested how these lighting qualities vary objectively, optically, in real conditions and whether they influence a social factor like the subjective, perceived friendliness of a face, and how well-lit a face and surroundings appeared. The results showed that how well-lit, friendly, and comfortable faces and environments were rated, did not correlate to light intensity. The results instead indicated the importance of factors related to the modelling effects of the lighting like diffuseness and light vector.

articleTitle: Addressing Gaseous Impurities in Packaged Laser Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Laser diodes used in non-lighting applications, such as telecommunication, automotive and augmented reality applications, are often hermetically sealed to protect these devices from possible damages due to atmospheric gases, harsh environment and dust, aiming for stable performances and longer lifetime. However, these sealed devices may experience issues caused by internal outgassing of gas species like H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and VOCs (Volatile Organic Compounds) released by inner materials or components. The new ZeDry® family getter solutions provide combined features in terms of improved gas sorption action, enhanced thermal and mechanical stability with anti-reflective coating properties. Indeed the new ZeDry® black getter coatings are effective in reducing scattered light and stray light, so improving the performances of the optical systems. ZeDry®-"black version" acts as an absorber of visible and IR wavelength light. New getter materials have been developed in order to sorb main detrimental gases and they are able to cope with high amounts of moisture, hydrogen and organic molecules.

articleTitle: Designing Metameric Light: Advanced Methods for Isolated Photoreceptor Response and Testing NIF Effects of Light
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Light does not only enable the visual system to perceive the outside world but it also impacts humans via non-visual processes such as regulating the circadian system or inducing instantaneous changes in alertness and mood. To be able to understand and quantify the effects of light on humans, we need sophisticated light designs that allow us to specifically target the desired photoreceptors. Experiments testing for the effects of light on human physiological and psychological processes have the caveat of using visually distinguishable light that hampers blinding participants to the experimental conditions and disentangling visual and non-visual processes. Metameric lighting might offer a solution to this challenge. In this paper, we propose an algorithmic approach using the principles of silent substitution and formulating it as an optimization problem to help researchers calculate metameric light pairs efficiently. Keywords— metameric light, ipRGCs, non-image-forming effects, silent substitution, tunable LEDs, optimization.

articleTitle: Consideration of Luminance Standard Values Based on Appropriate Contrasts Between Desk Illuminance and The Average Luminance of The Space
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: In Japan, the Academic Standard for Lighting Environment (AIJES-L0002-2016) was established by the Architectural Institute of Japan in 2016 [1]. After several years of practical application, its revision is now under discussion. This standard specifies recommended minimum average luminance values for ceiling and wall surfaces. However, the internal reflectance values on which these recommendations are based are set quite low to accommodate diverse design requirements, leading to concerns about excessive contrast relative to the illuminance of work surfaces. This study revisits the assumptions regarding interior reflectance and proposes an updated luminance standard to improve lighting design practices.

articleTitle: Preserving Visual Comfort in Office Spaces: Utilizing Digital Building Twins
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Visual comfort in office buildings is a crucial aspect of asset management. Achieving visual comfort involves a balanced combination of daylight and electric light. Efficiently evaluating visual comfort both subjectively and objectively (i.e., through surveys and lighting measurements) and dynamically communicating these assessments with an asset manager, building occupants, and other stakeholders presents significant challenges. Digital Twin (DT) technology has proven valuable in automating building management but has received less attention in the visual comfort field. This study proposes a fundamental DT architecture to efficiently evaluate visual comfort and light conditions in office environments. The DT framework integrates objective lighting measurements and occupant feedback, linking those to a virtual model using the linked data approach. A case study conducted in Eindhoven, the Netherlands, demonstrated that leveraging digital twins provides valuable insights into office workers’ visual comfort. This approach facilitates the identification of areas where occupants experience visual discomfort and detects spaces where lighting conditions (i.e., illuminance and Daylight Glare Probability) do not meet targeted thresholds. The proposed solution is prototyped in a web-based tool to demonstrate the model’s capabilities and allows for interactive engagement.

articleTitle: Preferred Illuminance at Different Correlated Color Temperatures for Paper- and Tablet-Based Reading Tasks in an Office Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: To understand the range of freedom that can be used for adjusting lighting levels with smart control algorithms in offices, we performed a laboratory study aimed to measure the preferred illuminance at different correlated color temperatures (CCTs) when performing reading tasks on paper and tablet. The experiment used a full-factorial three-by-two (i.e., 3 CCT × 2 task medium) within-subject design. Thirty-two participants could either decrease or increase the output of the ceiling luminaires to a preferred illuminance for each reading medium. In addition, three repetitions were included to understand how consistent participants were when indicating their preferred illuminance. The results show that both CCT and task medium have a significant effect on the preferred illuminance. We found a higher preferred illuminance for reading on paper than for reading on a tablet, and a higher illuminance for cool-white than for warm-white light. The range of spread in preferred illuminance was (averaged over all participants) about 250 lx, and larger than the difference in preferred illuminance between task medium and CCT.

articleTitle: Similarity Between Natural and Artificial Lights: Weighting by the Vision of Three Species of Heterocera
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Light pollution, a growing ecological concern, significantly impacts moths, which are crucial for pollination and biodiversity. This study compares artificial and natural light using the Daylight Similarity Index (DSI) and Moonlight Similarity Index (MSI). Spectral data from LED lamps and natural sources were weighted by the visual responses of three moth species. Maximum similarity was found at Correlated Color Temperature (CCT) between 3000–4000 K, which could be perceived as the most similar to natural light by insects. The findings suggest visual perception mechanisms are related to family rather than lifestyle, recommending further research with UV-inclusive light and other light characteristics.

articleTitle: LISN’s Effect on Electromagnetic Interference and DM Filter in Two-Stage AC/DC Flyback PFC Boost LED Driver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: AC/DC conversion is widely used in various applications, such as to power televisions, telephones, vehicles, LED lighting, and so on. Despite the popularity of AC/DC conversion, it presents problems related to electrical power quality (THD, power factor) as well as electromagnetic interference. To improve power quality and reduce interference, AC/DC conversion is continually being developed using new topologies. Among the most common topologies is the PFC Boost Flyback (power factor improvement and THD reduction). Nevertheless, these converters still exhibit electromagnetic interference and may exceed the limits of EMC standards. In this article, we simulate a two-stage PFC Boost Flyback AC/DC converter, operating as a LED driver, to determine the electrical quantities at the driver's input and output. Next, we analyze conducted disturbances exceeding EMC limits in the frequency range [150 kHz-30 MHz]. In this context, we have studied and designed a DM passive EMC filter to reduce these emissions, in compliance with EN55015 Class B standards.

articleTitle: Light Pollution Caused by Railway Station Lighting Systems - Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This paper deals with the radiation of outdoor lighting systems on railways. Due to the number and size of railway stations and their areas, these can contribute significantly to the increase of "light pollution" through the radiation of their luminous flux into the upper hemisphere. Outdoor lighting systems on railways behave de-facto like road lighting systems, but they are usually not taken into account as a significant contributor to light pollution and are of little interest.The aim of the paper is to show, by the example of the behaviour of a small railway station, the changes in the behaviour of the luminous flux in a given small railway station. The findings address whether new LED-based lighting systems, which respect all normative recommendations not only in terms of the required light technical parameters in the visual task areas, but especially in terms of the requirements for minimizing direct radiation into the upper hemisphere, are really better than the physically and morally obsolete lighting systems implemented 20 to 40 years ago, dominated by luminaires equipped with high-pressure sodium lamps. The paper discusses not only the light technical parameters, but also the power input parameters and the number of luminaires that are necessary to achieve the normative requirements, which result not from environmental requirements, but from safety requirements.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Control and Management System for Smart Street Lighting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This work focuses on the real-time monitoring of a public lighting system powered by a photovoltaic source. A graphical interface has been developed to display sensor data, allowing real-time monitoring and control of this system. The results evaluate the accuracy and reliability of the sensor network, which is crucial for optimizing energy efficiency in public lighting. The monitoring concerns the electrical parameters of the lamps such as voltage, current, power, energy. In addition, the weather data is also displayed (irradiance, and temperature) in order to control the photovoltaic system powering the proposed lighting system.

articleTitle: Biomaterial Based Transport Layer for Organic Light Emitting Diode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The demand for compact, efficient, and biocompatible Organic Light Emitting Diodes (OLEDs) is rising, especially for bio-photonic applications like imaging, investigating, and treating living matter with light. OLED technology is mature enough to meet these needs, but medical applications also require biocompatible materials, sometimes even bio-based ones. Integrating biomolecules within OLEDs can reduce embedded energy and the carbon footprint. However, creating biomaterial-based OLEDs is challenging due to performance, fabrication, stability, and durability issues. This paper focuses on integrating biomolecule-based Transport Layer within OLEDs, specifically using carotenoid material. The study involves DFT quantum modeling to determine the structural properties of carotenoids, SILVACO TCAD for numerical modeling, and optimization of the structure to achieve the best performance.

articleTitle: Algorithms for Personalized Lighting Control Using Well-Being Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The use of adaptive lighting systems, which are designed to target an individual's psychophysiological state, represents a promising avenue for enhancing employee health and well-being. Notwithstanding the significant advancements in our comprehension of the non-visual impacts of lighting on human, no algorithms have been devised for practical applications that utilize human state data. This longitudinal study was conducted over a period of eight months in the working polyclinic. Psychological surveys and biometric monitoring data were used in combination. Heart rates were considered for further integration into the control of lighting systems. The results demonstrated that heart rate correlate with human performance and can be utilized in the proposed lighting control algorithms.

articleTitle: The Impact of Daytime Lighting Conditions on Sleepiness and Morning/Evening Melatonin Levels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Proper lighting adjustments can reduce energy consumption in buildings, particularly by supporting thermal comfort and minimizing reliance on heating and cooling systems. This study explores the impact of office lighting on sleepiness and melatonin levels, contributing to a broader understanding of lighting’s impacts on human health and wellbeing. Twenty participants were exposed to various lighting conditions over five consecutive working days, with repeated measurements providing insights into the influence of artificial lighting on sleepiness and daily melatonin fluctuations. Results showed that lighting conditions did not significantly affect sleepiness during the experimental period (8:40–15:15). While no immediate melatonin response was observed, longer-term exposure to warm white light for two days resulted in lower melatonin levels at 20:00 and bedtime compared to one-day exposure. Morning melatonin levels decreased throughout the experiment, likely due to the absence of daylight in the office setting.

articleTitle: Lighting as a Means to Accentuate and Encourage The Reuse of Buildings in the Public Space: the Case of Historic Building of the Athens Home for the Elderly
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Is there a connection between a building's function and its façade lighting? Is lighting capable of awakening the collective memory of the city? Inspired by these questions, the research focuses on the upgrade of a building’s façade through lighting, and investigates the existence of a correlation between a building’s architectural identity and the type of façade lighting chosen for it. In this context, this research attempts to explore whether it is possible to accentuate architecture and breathe new life into abandoned spaces using artificial lighting and encourage the reuse of buildings.

articleTitle: Net-Zero Building Lighting: A Smart Lighting System Framework Enabled by Photovoltaic-Integrated Power over Ethernet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: As we enter the fourth industrial revolution, characterized by the ‘Digital-Intelligent Revolution’ and the integration of information and energy, the demand for efficient and intelligent energy management has become increasingly urgent. Traditional high-voltage lighting networks, with their cumbersome frameworks, struggle to meet these growing energy efficiency demands. This paper introduces a novel photovoltaic-integrated power over ethernet (PPoE) lighting framework for buildings, which not only reduces energy consumption but also enhances the overall performance of the smart lighting system. By seamlessly integrating energy and data, PoE optimizes the responsiveness and adaptability of the lighting network through multimodal sensing. The adoption of low-voltage DC photovoltaic energy enables direct powering of lighting, significantly reducing energy losses and contributing to net-zero carbon emissions. This innovative combination of power supply methods and smart lighting provides essential improvements in efficiency, sustainability, and human-centric control, marking a major advancement in sustainable building technologies.

articleTitle: Does Good Lighting Draw us Into a Room? Examining the Relationship Between Visual Features, Subjective Light Quality, and Approach-Avoidance in Indoor Environments Using Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This study examines the relationship between approach-avoidance responses (i.e., our willingness to approach a space), perceived presence of daylight and light quality, and objective visual features (color, contrast, presence of windows and luminaires) using image analysis of 212 photographs of indoor environments. Results showed that objective visual features explained 48% and 49% of the variance in the perceived presence of daylight and light quality, respectively. Light quality and perceived presence of daylight showed a high intercorrelation and were both positively related to approach, particularly light quality. Lastly, light quality mediated the relationship between visual features and approach-avoidance. These findings extend our understanding of the relationship between lighting and approach-avoidance responses and showcase the proposed method of image analysis for lighting research.

articleTitle: Dependence of Visibility of a Fallen Object in a Tunnel on Vehicle Moving Speed
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: We evaluated the visibility of fallen objects on the road while a vehicle is moving in a tunnel and evaluated its speed dependence. The experiments were done in the national full-scale tunnel for experimental evaluation. The results show that the distance from a subject to a fallen object on a road when the subject recognised the fallen object is proportional to the natural logarithm of the luminance ratio between the fallen object and the background road surface. The slope of the logarithm line is constant, independent of the vehicle speed. The slope is larger in the reverse silhouette-view condition than in the silhouette-view condition. Consequently, at least in the speed range of 40-80 km/h, the visibility depends on the luminance ratio between the fallen object on the road and the background road surface. Improving the visibility of a fallen object on a road in a tunnel by increasing the ratio of luminance between the surface of the fallen object and the road surface is more effective for silhouette viewing than for inverse silhouette viewing. We conclude that from the viewpoint of visibility, the asphalt road, which gives a reverse silhouette view, is better than the concrete road.

articleTitle: LEDs Spectrum Optimization: an Exercise in Non-Linear Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The properties of a mix of spectra, like typically produced by the association of colored LEDs, are described by a few indicators taking into account the Human visual perception. Smart lighting systems will f.i. offer control in terms of level (illumination) and Correlated Color Temperature. This paper is about illustrating the various relationships between those indicators for a mix of red, green, and blue LEDs. It also emphasizes on implementing the optimization procedure to maximize the lamp utility and checking the validity of the computed operating points. The influence of a few degrees of freedom will also be evaluated numerically.

articleTitle: Standalone Electrolytic-Capacitor-Less Universal Input Voltage LED Driver based on Parallel Integrated Converters using Variable Inductance to Compensate Input Voltage Variation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This paper presents an electrolytic-capacitor-less LED driver. The driver is made up by the integration of two converters in parallel. The first converter is a Buck-boost used to deliver constant current to the LED load, named as Power Control (PC) stage, while working as power factor correction meanwhile. The parallel converter is a Boost employed to reduce the ripple in the LED current, named as Ripple Reduction (RR) stage. This integration creates the Integrated Parallel Buck-Boost and Boost Converter (IPB3C), which shows great performance. However, the variation of any operation parameter affects both the efficiency and ripple reduction. Thus, creating a universal input voltage range driver is not straightforward. This paper proposes a variable inductor solution that will control both circulating power and ripple reduction percentages and eliminates the effect of the input voltage range variation.

Author Keywords: integrated parallel buck-boost and boost converter

articleTitle: Modelling Office Lighting Optimization for Daylight Saving Time Transitions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Modern indoor lifestyles, where individuals spend up to 87% of their time indoors, emphasize the importance of artificial lighting in supporting circadian health. Light serves as a critical environmental cue to synchronize the body internal clock with the 24-hour solar cycle. However, limited exposure to natural light in office settings can disrupt circadian alignment, particularly during Daylight Saving Time (DST) transitions, which advance or delay clocks by one hour. These transitions often result in circadian misalignment, causing sleep disturbances, reduced productivity, and impaired well-being.This study employs mathematical modeling and optimization to develop office lighting profiles that accelerate circadian adaptation during DST transitions. Simulations with a virtual cohort of 200 individuals demonstrate significant reductions in adaptation time. For spring transitions, optimized lighting reduced adaptation times from 10.8 ± 4.7 days to 5.5 ± 3.9 days. For autumn transitions, adaptation times decreased from 9.8 ± 0.2 days to 5.2 ± 0.3 days. Our results highlight the effectiveness of tailored morning light exposure to facilitate phase shifts.The findings provide valuable insights for designing adaptive lighting systems that mitigate the adverse side effects of DST transitions. Beyond DST, the proposed optimization framework provides insights for other circadian disruptions, such as jet lag and shift work. By establishing a robust mathematical approach, this work contributes to circadian rhythm research and offers a foundation for creating human-centric lighting strategies that enhance well-being and productivity in indoor environments.

articleTitle: Light Exposure Profiles Among Students: Exploring Adherence to Light Hygiene Recommendations and Implications for Sleep
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Light can have a profound impact on human sleep and daytime functioning. Therefore, adopting and maintaining healthy light hygiene is essential. This study employed ecological momentary assessment to investigate 24/7 light exposure profiles within a student sample. Adherence to the recent recommendations for healthy light exposure profiles by Brown et al. [1] was inspected. Additionally, we explored associations between the degree of adherence to these recommendations and sleep. The results showed substantial interindividual and intraindividual differences in daily light exposure profiles, with frequent instances of non-adherence to the recommendations. Light exposure during the daytime (in time above 250 m-EDI lux) predicted sleep quality during the subsequent night on weekend days. Methodological challenges and opportunities are discussed.

articleTitle: RADYNVR: a Radiance Tool for Simulating Dynamic Natural Lighting for VR Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Light impacts how we perceive environments, with recent studies focusing on the perception of dynamic luminous patterns of natural light. Immersive virtual reality is valuable for such studies since it offers complete control over the lighting in an environment. However, tools for generating virtual environments with dynamic natural lighting are limited. To address this, we present RADYNVR (Radiance Dynamic Virtual Reality), a simulation tool that offers an accurate and straightforward method to create virtual environments with dynamic natural lighting using Radiance. Key features of the tool are the ability to create shadow patterns of leaves swaying in the wind, and the efficient and accurate simulation of two characteristics of sunlight, solar penumbras and pinhole projections.

articleTitle: UGR Calculation Methods Reliability Investigation for LED Luminaires
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: In pursuit of energy efficiency goals, LEDs have been widely adopted, though considerations of discomfort remain crucial. LED luminaires with non-uniform luminous intensity distribution (LID), seems contribute to visual discomfort, particularly glare, assessed through the Unified Glare Rating (UGR) index. Although UGR index updates e.g., CIE 232:2019 offer technics to improve UGR calculation for non-uniform LID and LED luminaires, through an investigation of two popular methods—software simulation and manual calculation—this research underscores substantial disparities and inconsistencies in outputs.

articleTitle: Balancing the Performance-Efficiency Trade-off in Lighting Control Systems through Meta-Optimisation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Occupancy-based lighting control systems provide dimming solutions according to the positions of occupants. Computational optimisation assists these systems in identifying dimming strategies that enhance energy efficiency. However, the parameters used in the optimisation process influence both the system’s processing time and the level of energy reduction achieved. This study used a meta-optimisation method to determine these parameters, balancing processing time and energy consumption. In a simulated realistic open-plan office environment, the Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II was used to evaluate a range of dimming optimisation parameters that varied in processing time and energy efficiency. The resulting optimal parameters allowed the lighting control system to effectively provide dimming solutions for dynamic occupancy scenarios, leading to improved energy savings.

articleTitle: An Embedded Hardware Development Pipeline for IoT-Based Multi-color Light Therapy Solutions in Depression Relief
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Single-color light therapy has substantial scientific evidence supporting its healing effects on depression. Recent experiments have also demonstrated the effectiveness of multi-color light therapy, which combines different light colors with adjustable intensity, color temperature, and exposure time, in alleviating depressive symptoms. To facilitate the implementation of such multi-color light therapy, we propose an IoT architecture designed to manage a combination of light parameters based on experimental setups. This framework includes emotion data sensing, data communicating, and light control, all implemented with a focus on usage safety and adjustability. Such framework integrating psychological support, multi-color light therapy, and its IoT implementation, defines an embedded hardware development pipeline for IoT-based multi-color light therapy solutions in depression relief.

articleTitle: Interlaboratory Comparison for Temporal Light Modulation Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The International Energy Agency (IEA) 4E SSL Annex has conducted an Interlaboratory Comparison (IC 2023) for the measurement of temporal light modulation (TLM) of solid-state lighting (SSL) products. Designed to meet proficiency testing requirements, IC 2023 compared measured TLM quantities of short-term flicker indicator $\left( {P_{{\text{st}}}^{{\text{LM}}}} \right)$ and stroboscopic effect visibility measure (SVM, MVS), as well as three other TLM quantities, of four comparison LED lamp artefacts. A comparison between the four Nucleus Laboratories was first conducted to establish reference values. The IC 2023 main round had 18 labs participate worldwide. The results showed much larger variations than expected. Analysis of the results identified the need for more robust test methods, with improvement in required performance specifications for TLM instruments, test equipment, and guidance on determining measurement uncertainties.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Luminaire Object Detection in Floorplans
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: We present a deep neural network (DNN) machine learning model to detect luminaire objects from custom floorplan images, which contain small luminaire objects, complex backgrounds, and varying degrees of occlusion. We explore various training strategies, DNN architecture designs, and optimization methods in the literature. We custom train and optimize these and experimentally show that YOLO-v8m gives the best performance-accuracy trade-off, achieving a mean average precision of 0.48, perfectly within acceptable limits of inference time on a standard desktop computer. This represents a substantial decrease in labor and costs compared to manually annotating the floorplans, which takes around 45 minutes for an average size floorplan for highly trained personnel.

articleTitle: The Use of LED Technology in Stage Lighting. A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Over the past two decades, international regulations on energy efficiency have led to the gradual replacement of incandescent, halogen and fluorescent lamps in favor of light-emitting diodes (LEDs). In the field of stage lighting, the replacement of traditional lighting with LEDs represents a revolution that raises numerous financial, technical, esthetic and artistic issues. The educational materials for lighting designers in the arts are rooted in 20th century practices and are now outdated. In this article, we conducted a literature review to update existing work on this topic. In doing so, we found that support for this transition is nascent and mainly serves informational, cautionary or educational purposes.

articleTitle: Power Consumption of a LiFi Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Improved energy efficiency is one of the challenges for a future-generation communication network. This paper addresses whether optical wireless communication can save energy in delivering high-speed internet access by using light to transmit data. Light Fidelity (LiFi) needs a more reliable model of the power consumed by an LED that is being modulated (Watt/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> per bit/s), i.e., one that is more reliable than commonly used in scientific literature. Many earlier publications stated that the optical power is proportional to the average intensity signal (1st moment), while the electrical power would be proportional to the variance, i.e., to the average of the square of the signal. This frequently made assumption for the electrical power is surprising, as it suggests that an light emitting diode (LED) can violate the Law of Conservation of Energy. It also ignores the Shockley diode equation and it fails to account for the energy needed to generate a photon. Nevertheless, many results and papers on LiFi borrow their solutions from radio frequency (RF), and have been optimized as if power is proportional to the variance. An LED differs from a 50 Ω antenna in non-linearity. Moreover, its performance depends on biasing. This paper proposes a more realistic power consumption model for LiFi.

articleTitle: Interactions of Light with Materials – Lighting Materials and Materializing Light
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Visual perception of materials is crucial for our interactions with the world around us, and understanding the optical and perceptual mechanisms behind it has applications from spectral tuning to holistic appearance tuning. How real materials appear optically is determined by the real light they are in and described by ecological optics. With formal psychophysical experiments we test the perception of their color and texture, how matte/glossy, rough/smooth, hard/soft, glittery, velvety, etcetera we perceive them to be – and how those percepts are related to the ecological optics. I will present a series of studies into light-material-interactions and material perception of computer rendered, real, and painted materials. In addition, I will present research into effects of materials on light, and how materials can be used to make spatial and form-giving qualities of light visible in empty space, using "light probes."

articleTitle: Origins and Ecological Relevance of International Obtrusive Light Thresholds
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Light pollution from outdoor lighting impacts astronomical observations, ecology, and human health, with its global increase threatening previously dark environments. This paper examines international obtrusive light thresholds, revealing that current standards are primarily human-centric and based on outdated light sources. Environmental lighting zones, initially designed for inhabited areas, lack the scope to safeguard sensitive ecosystems. Analysis shows that current zones and thresholds need restructuring to include ecological considerations, particularly for conservation areas where species can be affected by very low light levels. Standards need updating to integrate ecological thresholds for effective environmental protection.

Author Keywords: ecological impacts of light at night

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Luminaire Detection in Professional Lighting Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This study evaluates vision-based deep learning models for real-time artificial light source detection on professional lighting images. We investigate detecting luminaires on (possibly embedded) edge devices and subsequently classifying them. The main challenges to overcome are the rather strict computational limitations of these devices, as well as the issues arising from image occlusion and reflections. We explore and compare various model training strategies, neural network architecture designs, and optimization methods. In our experiments, YOLOv-9t achieves a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.65 at 86 fps, a 54.76% performance increase compared to feature-based model performance on edge cases.

articleTitle: Leakage Inductance Reduction in Coupled Inductors Used in Quasi-Resonant Flyback Converters as LED Drivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This paper presents the demonstration of a method for reducing leakage inductance in coupled inductors used in quasi-resonant flyback converters as LED drivers, and its impact on converter efficiency. It briefly explains the leakage inductance effects in flyback converters and discusses methods to mitigate the flux leakage in coupled inductors. The interleaving technique is applied to eleven inductor models with similar characteristics but different winding structures, and results are compared through theoretical calculation and practical measurements. The best results show a reduction in the switch voltage peak from 629V to 533V and an increase in efficiency from 86,77 % to 91,5 %, along with a significant decrease in components temperatures, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method at improving converter’s performance and lifespan without additional components.

articleTitle: Catastrophic degradation of LEDs: failure analysis and perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: With this work we will report on catastrophic degradation of high power LEDs for general lighting, horticulture, and automotive. Results indicate that while gradual degradation is limited at mild driving condition, catastrophic degradation can arise suddenly as the stress condition increases. The presented results illustrate failure analysis of encapsulant, package, and chip of white and monochromatic LEDs and perspectives to limit these issues.

articleTitle: Characterizing the Accuracy of the Current CIE-standard and Cone-fundamental-based Spectral Luminous Efficiency Functions based on Achromatic Brightness Matches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The predictive accuracy of the CIE 2015 cone-fundamental-based spectral luminous efficiency functions (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F2</inf>(λ) and V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F10</inf>(λ)) and the CIE 1924 2° V(λ) and 1964 10° V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>(λ) functions were evaluated based on visual data from 54 observers in a 10° brightness and color (achromatic) matching experiment using eight different LED primaries. The CIE 2015 10° V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F10</inf>(λ) and 1964 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>(λ) functions outperformed the CIE 2° V(λ) functions, particularly in the cyan region. However, for primaries at 520 nm and 404 nm, the 2° V(λ) functions provided slightly more accurate luminance predictions than the 10° functions. The 673 nm deep red primary resulted in greater variability in matching brightness. Older observers exhibited similar trends to younger observers but with larger variations in brightness matching.

articleTitle: The Development of Personalized Visual Comfort Prediction Models Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This study extends the framework of personal thermal comfort models to visual comfort prediction using machine learning. In the course of the experiment, twelve participants experienced three thermal and five lighting conditions over five consecutive working days, each evaluating visual comfort 140 times. Survey responses and measured environmental and physiological data revealed individual differences in comfort ratings, supporting the need for personalized lighting. Prediction models based on environmental conditions achieved up to 82% accuracy, while those using physiological responses reached 68%. Despite limitations in the variety of lighting conditions and a low frequency of pupil size measurements, the findings highlight a promising approach for personalized lighting solutions integrating personal preferences and environmental dynamics.

articleTitle: Verification of the Inactivation Effect of Near-UV LEDs using a Pulsed Lighting System on Staphylococcus aureus
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the disinfection effect of Near-UV LED light, which is pulsed using PWM control, on Staphylococcus aureus. To evaluate the disinfection effect of Near-UV LED light, three types of Near-UV LEDs with wavelengths of 395 nm, 385 nm, and 365 nm were installed within a sealed space inside an incubator and energized with a forward current of 1000 mA and a forward voltage of 3.6 V, and the disinfection rate under each type of light was assessed. Additionally, the disinfection effect was evaluated when the same three types of Near-UV LEDs were pulsed with a 50% duty cycle. As a result, 100% disinfection was achieved with 365 nm Near-UV LED direct-current irradiation for 120 seconds, and a 93% disinfection rate was obtained with pulsed irradiation for 150 seconds.

articleTitle: Leveraging Language Models for Human Activity Recognition for Intelligent Lighting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Recognizing human activities is necessary to achieve fully context-aware lighting in a smart home. Ambient sensors suit this task as they are ubiquitous, non-intrusive, and non-obstructive. However, each home has a unique floor plan and a unique number and placement of these sensors. This leads to heterogeneity of input data spaces for machine learning models, which hinders their use in different homes. We propose that converting the data into the semantic input space of a language model can not only unify the input space across different houses but also improve the prediction performance thanks to the model’s understanding of semantics. We compared a pre-trained BERT model with one trained from scratch to test the proposed semantic conversion on three datasets from CASAS. The results show that the pre-trained model performs better on accuracy and F1-score.

articleTitle: The Environmental Impact of Sensors in Smart Lighting Systems: Enhancing the Lighting as a Service (LaaS) Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The transition to a circular economy aims to minimize waste and preserve resources. Lighting as a Service (LaaS) is a model that aligns with the principles of circularity, by providing lighting solutions that may reduce environmental impact and promote sustainability. As lighting technologies have become more sophisticated, LaaS Models have developed smart lighting systems using motion sensors and hubs which, by reducing the duration of use, result in lower energy consumption. Studies carried out a few years ago indicated that although sensors and hubs were capable of saving energy, their standby consumption resulted in higher consumptions. Recently, new generation sensors and hubs with low standby consumption emerged. Thanks to this, the environmental performance of smart lighting systems is improved, according to new measurements, guaranteeing a comfortable user experience.

articleTitle: Naturalness Bias Revisited: Effect of Source Attribution on the Restorative Potential of Abstract Dynamic Light Patterns With Natural and Non-Natural Movement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Literature shows that we prefer lighting that we consider to be natural, exhibiting a "naturalness bias". It was also shown that attributing the source of an ambiguous audio stimulus to nature may increase the restorative potential of the stimulus compared when the source is attributed to a non-natural origin. The current study examines the influence of source attribution on the perceived restoration potential of abstract light patterns with natural and non-natural movement. To this end, we conducted an online experiment with 121 participants using videos depicting dynamic light patterns projected on the wall of an office environment and instructed participants that the dynamic light patterns came from nature or a computer algorithm. Results show that natural movement led to higher perceived restoration potential compared to non-natural movement, although both conditions were rated very low in perceived naturalness. On the other hand, neither source attribution nor its interaction with movement influenced the perceived restoration potential. However, when only the natural movement data stimuli were analyzed, source attribution did significantly (negatively) affect the preference and perceived stressfulness ratings, and marginally influenced perceived restoration potential. These findings suggest that the mere cognitive attribution of an abstract dynamic stimulus to a natural source is not sufficient to increase its restorative potential.

articleTitle: Interlaboratory Comparison On Traceable Flicker And Stroboscopic Effect Measurements Of Light Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Temporally modulated light emitting diodes (LEDs) can influence comfort, health and safety. Therefore, the European Commission introduced Ecodesign requirements with respect to temporal light modulation (TLM). To accommodate measurements of these TLM metrics, SI traceability for TLM measurement methods has been developed, which has been validated in an interlaboratory comparison. Eight participants measured the flicker and stroboscopic effect of eleven artefacts. The results show artefact stability and comparing the degrees of equivalence against a comparison reference value based on the mean of the participant measurements. Most lamps were stable, and the flicker and stroboscopic effect values were overall in good consensus, except some outliers which could have been the result of underestimation of uncertainty of some individual participants, differences in algorithm and systematic errors by individual participants.

articleTitle: Solid-State Lighting: Health Effects and Knowledge Gaps
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The health effects of LED lamps and luminaires used for general lighting were reviewed by an international team of researchers working under the 4E implementing agreement of the International Energy Agency (SSLC platform). Effects on the general population and subsets of sensitive groups were studied considering interactions with eye and skin, glare, circadian regulation, neuro-behavioral effects, effects of temporal light modulation, and long-term effects, such as age-related macular degeneration, myopia, and risks of cancer. This paper presents the conclusions and recommendations of the expert group. Knowledge gaps are detailed in each effect category.

articleTitle: Study on the Relationship Between Window Specifications and Occupants' Assessment of Light and Visual Environment in Japanese Housing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: A questionnaire survey on window specifications and room impressions was conducted with the aim of proposing a method for evaluating the performance and function of the light and visual environment provided by the presence of windows in Japanese housing. The results of the factor analysis of the questionnaire survey revealed that the occupants' evaluations can be categorized into daylighting satisfaction, viewability, light/dark difference in the room and openness. The correlation between window specifications and questionnaire results indicated that lighting satisfaction could be estimated using relatively straightforward inputs, such as the degree of sky visibility and the absolute window area.

articleTitle: Mapping After-dark Urban Environments: Aerial Surveying for Data Integration and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a georeferenced after-dark map of a university campus, covering approximately an area of 1 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, created through nighttime aerial surveying. The map was reconstructed from 894 photographs and georeferenced to enable further data integration and spatial analysis. After that, the collected data were processed to calculate luminance and detect lighting features using advanced techniques such as computer vision and machine learning. This study serves as an initial step towards future advancements and applications in urban lighting research and practice, supporting the importance of balancing the benefits of nighttime illumination with its potential adverse effects.

articleTitle: Examining the Impact of Aging of the Lighting Equipment and the New Revision of Lighting Standards on a Football Lighting Pitch
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to capture the lighting requirements of a football pitch according to the current international standards for lighting of football matches and the UEFA regulations, and how these have changed over the last 15 years. For the specific football stadium studied, whose lighting was designed in 2011 according to the regulations in force at the time a) the qualitative and quantitative parameters of the standards were considered and b) these parameters were compared with their respective values measured under real stadium lighting conditions in 2024. From the comparison of the measured quantities with those of the standards as well as the regulations of different time periods, conclusions were drawn regarding the impact of the maintenance of the lighting system and the degradation of the visual comfort and television image quality with respect to both the previous and the amended and newer current standards. Also, conclusions were drawn as per how the amendment of standards affects the visual effect compared to the older standards.

articleTitle: Effects of Smart Adaptive Street Lighting on Residents’ Behavior and Experiences: Results from a Field Test
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Adaptive street lighting uses sensor technology to adapt luminance output to street activity to reduce energy consumption and light pollution. However, little is known about how residents experience and are affected by such systems. Therefore, qualitative data were collected via diaries with follow-up interviews, and a focus group amongst residents of a neighborhood in which adaptive street lighting had recently been installed. Using thematic analyses, three themes were extracted from the data. First, residents noticed the change in illumination from inside the home, creating a new kind of light pollution: light startle. Second, some residents used the lighting system for monitoring street activity—or at least had the urge to know who or wat activated the lighting. Third, the complex control algorithm did not afford residents in their competence to determine what caused the change in illumination. This in turn resulted in feelings of anxiety with at least one participant. Limitations and implications of these findings are discussed.

articleTitle: Decoding Lighting in Real and Virtual Environments: An EEG-Based Analysis of Emotional States
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of lighting conditions on emotional and cognitive states in real (RE) and virtual reality (VR) environments using the method of electroencephalography (EEG). By leveraging EEG wave bands—Alpha, Beta Low, and Gamma—we examine how neural activity varies under different lighting scenarios, including daylight (DL) and daylight combined with electrical lighting (DL+EL), and across two different conditions: scene experience (EXP) and performing activity (ACT). The paper explores methodologies for quantifying emotional arousal and valence using EEG-derived metrics. Arousal is calculated as a function of Gamma, Beta Low, and Alpha wave amplitudes to capture cognitive engagement and alertness. Emotional valence is assessed through frontal alpha asymmetry, measuring lateralized activity in the brain’s frontal regions to evaluate the polarity of emotional states. By comparing these metrics across RE and VR under different conditions, the study aims to provide insights into the neural and emotional dynamics of lighting perception and its implications for both real and simulated environments. This work bridges neuroscience, environmental psychology, and virtual reality design, offering a comprehensive framework for evaluating the emotional and cognitive effects of lighting in diverse settings.

articleTitle: Enhancing LED Cooling Efficiency Through wind ionic Technology: A Numerical Analysis of Point-to-Plane and Line-to-Plane Configurations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: LEDs are widely used and cover all possible applications of artificial lighting, both for low power in domestic lighting and for very high power such as stadium or airport lighting. In the case of high-power lighting, thermal management is a crucial element because it seriously affects energy efficiency but above all the life of the light source. Several cooling techniques exist (heat pipe, fan, etc.) but the use of ionic winds for cooling LEDs has many interesting advantages (no moving mechanical parts, high energy efficiency, etc.). This study provides a numerical analysis of this innovative cooling technology using ionic wind, by comparing two possible configurations: point-to-plane and line or wire-to-plane. The results present the cooling efficiencies associated with the two cases studied.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition In Time Series In PIR Sensor Networks With Reinforcement Learning For Smart Lighting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Recognizing human activity from IoT events is essential for automatic light scene setting. A challenge with IoT systems is the diversity among customers. For addressing this diversity a reinforcement learning method is explored that enables for each customer the learning of a model for classifying context of time series. The method is a Bayesian method and it is of interest as a prior is put on the states that are to be predicted. Results on activity recognition will be given for a household and the relative feature-importance of time-of-the-day versus motion will be analyzed.

articleTitle: Challenges and Solutions on the Road Towards Smart Lighting with Projected LED Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Dynamic illumination systems with an adaptive radiation pattern can be realized by combining high-resolution LED arrays with suitable projection optics. If such adaptive lighting fixtures are furthermore combined with one or more camera sensors, smart lighting systems can be developed. Such systems are already in use for automotive applications, i.e. for adaptive exterior car lighting, but have not yet been commercialized for general lighting. In this paper some important challenges and potential solutions are discussed on the road towards smart lighting with projected LED arrays for general lighting applications.

articleTitle: Exploring Pedestrian's Visual Attention and Walkability Preference in Nighttime Commercial Street Using Eye-Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This study explores the relationship between pedestrian's visual attention and walkability preference in nighttime commercial street, using East Nanjing Road in Shanghai as a case study. Eye-tracking data were collected from 46 participants viewing 34 images with walkability preferences assessed through self-reports. Environmental elements were identified and categorized using semantic recognition and the images were divided into high-walkability preference (HWP) and low-walkability preference (LWP) groups. Differences in fixation duration, fixation count, and information density (calculated as the ratio of subjective fixation proportion to objective area proportion) were analyzed. Results show that buildings attracted the longest fixation duration and the most fixation counts, followed by people among all images. Across both groups, lighting elements exhibited high information density, buildings had medium density, while green plants and the sky showed relatively low density. Notable differences emerged between groups, with participants in the LWP group paying more visual attention to advertisements. This study provides insights into pedestrians' visual attention in nighttime commercial streets, informing the design of urban walking environments after dark.

articleTitle: Closer to Realtime: A Comparison of Machine Learning Methods to Reduce Artificial Switch-Off Times
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Presence-based control of artificial lighting is an important method of reducing energy consumption for artificial lighting. Passive infrared sensors are the most commonly used detection technology due to their low investment costs and simple commissioning. However, these are typically tied to switch-off times to reduce nuisance false-off rates. If the switch-off times are set too long, this can impair energy efficiency. Probabilistic methods make it possible to reduce switch-off times based on real occupancy patterns. In order to automate this process and take seasonal effects into account, various machine learning-based modelling approaches are compared. The basis is a high-resolution data set from an open-plan office. The results show that the modelling approaches are highly accurate in predicting periods of inactivity and thus create a solid basis for deriving suitable time-variant switch-off times. This is reflected in a lower energy requirement.

articleTitle: Smart Street Lighting Systems for Sustainable Smart Cities: A Conceptual Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The rapid growth of urban population has significantly complicated urban planning and management. This paper examines the connected street lighting network as an innovative infrastructure solution for smart cities by integrating cutting-edge technologies into widespread street lighting network systems. Through a comprehensive literature review and expert consultancy, the study categorizes the predominant components of smart street lighting (SSL) and evaluates their potential contribution to sustainability and urban digital transformation. Among global researchers, China, Spain, and India stand out as the leading countries in this field. Furthermore, it is enhanced that the proposed connected lighting network not only increases the energy efficiency of cities and reduces their carbon footprint, but also contributes significantly to the improvement of human and ecological quality of life and the effective monitoring of various urban planning services. The study inferred that a connected street lighting system affects all six key smart city dimensions with the most substantial contribution (30%) to the smart living dimension. Additionally, the system aligns with nine of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), most prominently supporting SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities).

articleTitle: Case Study on the Effect of a Human-Centered Smart Lighting System on the Comfort Preferences of Office Workers with Different CCTs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This study examines the impact of human-centric lighting (HCL) in an open-plan office at Istanbul Technical University, involving 24 participants. The design process included circadian lighting metrics and simulation tools, focusing on varying Correlated Color Temperatures (CCTs) and their influence on visual comfort and satisfactions. The experiment used a wireless automation system to adjust lighting conditions and collect data on visual cognitive performance and preferences through questionnaires and performance tests. The results showed that a CCT of 2700K positively impacted participants, enhancing vertical illuminance and reducing task errors compared to 3800K and 6000K. Some dissatisfaction was reported with the 6000K setting. The study suggests that individualized, user-controllable lighting systems can improve office workers' satisfaction and cognitive performance, proposing the integration of energy-efficient, human-centered lighting systems in open-plan offices.

articleTitle: Feasibility Analysis of an Energy Storage System Without Batteries for Isolated Street Lighting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This paper investigates the feasibility of non-battery energy storage systems for isolated street lighting, focusing on mechanical storage technologies such as gravity storage, compressed air energy storage, and flywheels. As the global shift toward renewable energy accelerates, the challenge of intermittency in sources like solar and wind becomes increasingly significant. Traditional batteries, while widely used, present limitations in cost, lifespan, and environmental impact. Mechanical storage systems offer promising alternatives, with potential for greater sustainability and efficiency. Through a detailed analysis and comparison of investment costs, this study evaluates the practicality and effectiveness of these non-battery solutions in providing reliable energy storage for a sustainable future.

articleTitle: Development of LED Lighting for Microalgae Propagation with Emission Spectrum Having Broader Emission Peaks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: In this study, we aimed to develop LED lighting with an emission spectrum effective for microalgae propagation, and fabricated LED lighting with Phosphor layer RGB, which has peaks in the red, green, and blue wavelength bands, and Phosphor layer RG’B’, which has broader peaks in the red, green, and blue wavelength bands. In order to examine the effect of microalgae propagation, Closterium ehrenbergii samples prepared at different dilution rates were irradiated with LED illumination light of Phosphor layer RG’B’ and Phosphor layer RGB, respectively, for 7 days, and their propagation rates were compared. The results of the experiment showed that Phosphor layer RG’B’ produced a higher propagation rate than Phosphor layer RGB.

articleTitle: Remote Activation System Design for Rural Street Luminaires Energized via Power Distribution Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: Outdoor lighting in rural areas is less developed than in urban areas. This may be due to rural areas being less prioritized for infrastructure investments, limited financial resources and difficult accessibility due to their remote location.
