In rural areas, inadequate lighting conditions, especially in the evening hours, increase security risks, cause accidents, and adversely affect the quality of life by causing restrictions in areas such as education and training activities, working hours and social life. To overcome all these issues, this study aims to provide a remote activation system to rapidly and confidently remove transient faults in rural power distribution lines due to physical causes such as tree branch contact, wind impact, fires and pollution. Furthermore, this study fills a significant gap in the literature. Based on the principle of measuring line impedance, this system, which can detect transient faults in the line of sodium vapor street luminaires and offers remote intervention with the designed interface, is equipped with GSM communication and Modbus RS485 motorized vending fuse.

articleTitle: 6D to 3D Camera Colorimetric Calibration for Assessment of Lighting Scenes : IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting Conference, 12-14 november 2024, Eindhoven University of Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: We propose a colorimetric calibration method associated with an imaging device (based on a camera, filter or coloured mirror) to obtain calibrated images of scenes illuminated by light sources emitting different spectra. Usually, color calibration is sensitive to metamerism. Rather than using a single RGB triplet for each image pixel, the main idea is to collect additional information, such as a second RGB triplet, and then use transformation (RGB1; RGB2 to XYZ). We present how to collect two RGB triplets using an imaging device, and the used transformation. Computation time is evaluated and an optimized way of performing calibration is discussed to enable calibration of videos. The proposed method can be extended to calibrate from (RGB1; RGB2) to any embedded spectral quantity (e.g. blue hazard) and can then be used to evaluate lighting scenes according to various criteria, for human, animal or plant response to light.

articleTitle: Sustainable Illumination as a Catalyst for Change: The Broader Impacts of the Ponto Iluminado Initiative
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The Ponto Iluminado Initiative, centred on sustainable lighting, has evolved significantly, impacting both the community and the scientific field. This article examines how the Initiative's actions, focused on lighting systems, promote socio-environmental benefits and scientific advancements. Starting with the implementation of Brazil's first bus stop powered by photovoltaic energy, it expanded into areas such as energy efficiency, waste management, water conservation, and environmental education, always with lighting as the central pillar. Educational activities include initiatives in schools and universities, promoting rational energy use and sustainability awareness, while also studying barriers in energy planning. The project also engages volunteers, teaching sustainability and efficiency practically, offering a new perspective on resource utilization.

articleTitle: Energy Saving and CO2 Reduction of Expressway Lighting: A Case Study in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This paper summarizes a study report on specifications and standards of LED road lighting and electrical infrastructure to enhance energy stability of expressway lighting in Thailand. Thai Industrial Standard Institute (TISI) has announced Thai recommendation for lighting of roads for motor and pedestrian traffic, TIS 2954-2019 which is based on CIE 115-2010. More reports on measurement and assessment on road lighting in Thailand are being carried out and undergoing. The main part of this work will focus on energy saving and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> reduction evaluation before and after lamp changing from high pressure sodium (HPS) lamps to light emitting diode (LED) lamps of expressway lighting. Results showed that LED lamps can help with energy saving in both power density and annual energy consumption indicators and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> reduction. However, proper road lighting design is required to meet various criteria.

articleTitle: Validation of a New Python-Based Indoor Channel Model for Visible Light Communication Using Color Shift Keying
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental validation of a new Python-based indoor channel model for Visible Light Communication using Color Shift Keying. Traditional Color Shift Keying models have notable limitations, such as not accounting for the spectral response of emitters, detectors, and walls, and lacking tools for simulating Wavelength Division Multiplexing-based Visible Light Communication systems. Our model addresses these issues by incorporating spectral response and multi-wavelength propagation, designed to optimize Visible Light Communication performance in indoor environments. Validated through measurements of illuminance, color coordinates, and inter-channel interference, the model demonstrates robust accuracy, offering a valuable tool for Visible Light Communication system design and optimization.

articleTitle: Intuitive Human-Light Interaction through Embedded ML: Evaluation of Infrared Array Sensor for Advanced Gesture Control in Smart Lighting Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: In an era where human-technology interaction is becoming increasingly intuitive, this paper presents an innovative approach to gesture control in smart lighting systems. Utilizing an 8x8 infrared sensor read by an on-chip library previously trained off-chip, this method enables precise and contactless lighting control. The paper critically examines the use of infrared arrays, with embedded machine learning models used to enhance accuracy and reliability. This technology promises seamless human-light interaction, not only improving user experience but also opening new possibilities for designing smart environments.

articleTitle: Thermal Convection of a High-Power LED Heat Sink - Analysis and Processing of Images Obtained by Schlieren Optics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: LED lighting occupies all sectors including high power ones. The most efficient systems today reach nearly 30% and it is necessary to evacuate the 70% of thermal losses to protect the LEDs and allow them to have a long life. Among the alternatives to natural convection cooling, two main forced convection modes are presented: by fan or by ionic wind. This work presents a comparative study of the thermal performances of three cooling methods applied to an LED heat sink: natural convection, ionic wind cooling and forced convection using a fan. Experiments were conducted at different LED power levels, using Schlieren imaging to visualize thermal flows and MATLAB for thermal image analysis. The results show that while the fan offers the best thermal performances, the ionic wind stands out for its quiet operation and compact design. This study highlights the importance of selecting the appropriate cooling method based on the specific requirements of each application.

articleTitle: Estimating The VIS-NIR Spectral BRDF Of A Material From A Photograph
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: We propose a deep learning approach to estimate the VIS-NIR spectral BRDF of a material from a photograph. Materials transmit and reflect light emitted by light sources and have a major impact on the energy performance of buildings and their appearance as perceived by users. Obtaining the spectral BRDF of a material from an RGB photograph is a practical way of gathering the data needed to simulate and optimize light sources (including natural light) in buildings. We present the spectral BRDF model we used, the database we built, the neural network architectures involved, and the results obtained. In particular, spectral reflectance over the range 780 nm - 1000 nm is estimated with a relative error of 4.1%, making an RGB camera a promising tool for estimating spectral VIS-NIR quantities when it does not itself capture wavelengths above 780 nm.

articleTitle: Experimental Characterization of LEDs Aiming at VLC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: The evolution of LED technology has expanded its utility to areas beyond illumination, notably in Visible Light Communication (VLC). Among the crucial factors for data transmission via light, the choice of light source is essential. This paper is dedicated to introducing a high-frequency LED model, a significant contribution to the field. The insights gained from this model can greatly enhance our understanding of the load dynamics and the influence of various LED load aspects on its dynamic, thereby paving the way for more efficient and reliable VLC systems.

articleTitle: Change Trend in the Lighting Environment for Nighttime Townscape on the Light Intensity of Streetlight and Self-Luminous Billboards in a Model Town
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference & Expo (LS24)
abstract: This paper reports on an experiment conducted to find the tendency of adjustment of the lighting intensity of streetlights and self-luminous billboard in a model street block in order to find the tendency of changes in the light environment due to lighting that forms the nighttime streetscape.
